s1.syndrome_frame: progressive lower extremity pain and swelling with erythema
salient_findings: worsening left lower extremity pain, swelling, and erythema
severe lower extremity pain causing dependence in activities of daily living
erythematous, ill-defined, and extremely tender plaques on the left lower extremity
key_facts: 83-year-old woman
presented with worsening left lower extremity pain, swelling, and erythema for the past few months
previously independent in activities of daily living 2-3 months ago
became fully dependent on her daughter due to severe lower extremity pain
no history of trauma, recent travel, fever, chills, nausea, or vomiting
medical history included stage I breast cancer in remission for 8 years
current medications included hydrochlorothiazide, gabapentin, montelukast, and albuterol
former tobacco smoker
received radiation followed by immunotherapy, previously treated with nivolumab and sotorasib
began new medication 3 months before presentation
lower extremity erythema began a couple of weeks after first cycle
bilateral lower extremities were hyperpigmented with significant pitting edema
left lower extremity had erythematous, ill-defined, and extremely tender plaques from toes to knee
right lower extremity had smaller indurated plaques on the posterior ankle
laboratory tests showed low hemoglobin, elevated mean corpuscular volume, and elevated C-reactive protein

shortlist.label: Lipodermatosclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: erythematous, ill-defined, and extremely tender plaques on the lower extremities, consistent with lipodermatosclerosis

shortlist.label: Chronic venous insufficiency
shortlist.why_kept: bilateral lower extremities were hyperpigmented with significant pitting edema, suggesting chronic venous insufficiency

shortlist.label: Cellulitis
shortlist.why_kept: erythema, swelling, and tenderness of the lower extremity, which are common symptoms of cellulitis

shortlist.label: Erythema nodosum
shortlist.why_kept: tender plaques on the lower extremities, which could be consistent with erythema nodosum

shortlist.label: Radiation dermatitis
shortlist.why_kept: history of radiation therapy, which could contribute to the development of radiation dermatitis

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of worsening left lower extremity pain, swelling, and erythema, along with hyperpigmentation and significant pitting edema, is consistent with lipodermatosclerosis. The absence of fever, chills, and other signs of infection, as well as the temporal relationship with the new medication, also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Chronic venous insufficiency
rejected.why: While the patient has signs of venous insufficiency, such as pitting edema, the presence of erythematous and tender plaques is more suggestive of lipodermatosclerosis.

rejected.label: Cellulitis
rejected.why: The absence of fever, chills, and other signs of infection makes cellulitis less likely.

rejected.label: Erythema nodosum
rejected.why: The patient's presentation is not typical of erythema nodosum, which is usually characterized by well-defined, tender nodules.

rejected.label: Radiation dermatitis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms began after starting a new medication, rather than after radiation therapy, making radiation dermatitis less likely.
